subject.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging

question: Should OpenClaw accept content-bound SQLite provenance as the permanent trust lifecycle for generated HTML after it is copied from the temp root into outbound media?
rationale: The code review found no narrow patch defect, but the change deliberately authorizes a new class of host-read HTML path and that security boundary cannot be accepted by automation alone.

options.title: Accept provenance lifecycle
options.body: Land the PR after exact-head CI/mergeability if a maintainer or security owner accepts sha256+size provenance over the already-read buffer as the trusted staging contract.

options.title: Request tighter lifecycle proof
options.body: Ask for targeted proof or small hardening such as TTL-bounded row cleanup or chunked pruning before accepting the new trust lifecycle.

options.title: Reject staged HTML trust
options.body: Close or replace this direction if maintainers want generated HTML to remain temp-root-only and prefer PDF or another artifact flow for Telegram delivery.

recommendation.title: Accept provenance lifecycle
recommendation.body: Land the PR after exact-head CI/mergeability if a maintainer or security owner accepts sha256+size provenance over the already-read buffer as the trusted staging contract.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the original trusted generated HTML host-read seam that the PR extends.
